newsitem.title: USA: Yamaichi to end aid to Ogawa Securities.
newsitem.headline: Yamaichi to end aid to Ogawa Securities.

text.p: Yamaichi Securities Co will notify its ailing affiliate Ogawa Securities Co that it will terminate aid to the affiliate on Thursday, Jiji Press news agency reported Wednesday.

In response, Ogawa Securities will inform the Ministry of Finance of its plan to discontinue business within the day, launching procedures for its voluntary disbandment, said the report in JiJi Press, which quoted "informed sources."
It would be the first voluntary termination of business by a securities agency under the licensing system for securities companies introduced in 1968, JiJi Press said.

The Japan Securities Dealers Association will withdraw up to two billion yen to protect all Ogawa Securities' client assets. This is the first withdrawal from a client protection fund since the fund's establishment in 1969, the sources were quoted as saying in JiJi Press.

Ogawa, based in Osaka, western Japan, was ordered by the Ministry of Finance to correct its management after it plunged into financial crisis due to margin stock trading troubles according to the JiJi Press report.
In the year to last March, the firm suffered a recurring loss of some 260 million yen, its sixth straight annual loss according to JiJi Press.
Its reconstruction had depended on whether Yamaichi, one of the Big Four Japanese brokerages, would give Ogawa financial assistance, including a capital infusion.
Yamaichi has apparently concluded that any assistance will not guarantee Ogawa's reconstruction and could affect Yamaichi's performance, the sources said.
